questionsToConsider: Who do you most need to hear from: loyal customers, people who stopped buying, or people who only know your name?
Which words do you hope people pick, and which ones would worry you if they came up often?
Which competitors should respondents have in mind when they compare, and should you name them?
What decision will this feed, such as a rebrand, a new campaign or a change to your service?
guide.howToUseResponses: Split every result by the first question before reading anything else, because a regular customer and someone who has only seen your ads are describing different brands. Count how often each word is picked in each group and compare that with the words you want to own. Then read the answers about what changed people's minds, since those name the specific moments that are building or damaging your reputation.
customizeSteps: Replace the word list with the qualities your brand is aiming for plus a few honest negatives, so the survey can tell you when you miss.
Rename the rows in the experience grid to the parts of your business people actually touch, such as delivery, the app or the store.
Send it to customers and share it more widely by link, then compare the groups in the dashboard or export the answers to CSV.

faqs.q: What is a brand perception survey?
faqs.a: It asks people what they think and feel about your brand: the qualities they associate with it, how much they trust it and how it compares with alternatives. It measures opinion, not just whether people recognise your name.

faqs.q: What questions should a brand perception survey include?
faqs.a: Ask how familiar the person is with you, which words describe you, how far they trust you, how you compare with alternatives and what experience shaped their view. Without the familiarity question, the rest is hard to interpret.

faqs.q: Should I survey people who have never bought from us?
faqs.a: Yes, they show you the impression your marketing creates on its own. This template lets them skip the questions about service and delivery that they could only guess at.

faqs.q: How often should I run a brand perception survey?
faqs.a: Once or twice a year works for most brands, plus before and after a rebrand or a big campaign. Keep the core questions the same so you can compare results over time.
